rules.title: CSV file is empty
rules.description: The file has no content: 0 bytes, or only a byte-order mark and/or whitespace.

rules.title: File is a binary format, not CSV text
rules.description: The leading bytes identify a binary format such as an Excel .xlsx/.xls workbook, PDF, ZIP or image. Export the sheet as 'CSV UTF-8 (Comma delimited)' instead.

rules.title: File contains NUL bytes
rules.description: The file contains NUL (0x00) bytes, typical of UTF-16 text or binary data. Row checks are skipped.

rules.title: UTF-8 byte-order mark present (accepted)
rules.description: A UTF-8 byte-order mark (EF BB BF) starts the file. Excel's 'CSV UTF-8' format writes one; StockMetaLint accepts it and excludes it from header names.

rules.title: Malformed CSV structure
rules.description: A record could not be parsed: for example an unterminated quoted field, text after a closing quote, or a field larger than 128 KiB. Parsing stops at the first malformed record; earlier rows are still checked.

rules.title: Record has the wrong number of fields
rules.description: A record has a different number of fields than the header. Unquoted commas inside Keywords are the usual cause: the whole keyword list must be one double-quoted cell. Rows with extra fields are not content-checked because their columns cannot be aligned reliably.

rules.title: Blank record between data rows
rules.description: A blank or all-empty record appears after the header. StockMetaLint skips it and does not count it as a data row, but other tools may count or reject it.

rules.title: Leading or trailing whitespace
rules.description: A cell starts or ends with whitespace. In Filename this can prevent exact asset matching.
rules.notes: The trim-whitespace fix never modifies Filename cells; rename consistently instead.

rules.title: Control character in a cell
rules.description: A cell contains a tab, line break or other control character (for example a multi-line title inside quotes).

rules.title: Text is not Unicode NFC
rules.description: Text is not in Unicode Normalization Form C, so visually identical strings can differ in bytes (common for accented names created on macOS).
rules.notes: The nfc fix applies to Title and Keywords only, never to Filename.

rules.title: Over a length limit when counted in UTF-16 units
rules.description: The value is within its limit in Unicode code points but over it in UTF-16 code units, which is what HTML form maxlength counts (emoji and other astral characters count as two).
rules.notes: Which unit Adobe's backend counts is not documented; this advisory flags the ambiguity.

rules.title: Filename is not portable across operating systems
rules.description: The filename uses characters or names that are invalid on Windows: < > : " | ? *, control characters, reserved device names such as CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1 or LPT1, or a trailing dot or space.

rules.title: Duplicate keyword in a row
rules.description: The same keyword appears more than once in a row, compared case-insensitively after collapsing whitespace. Original spellings and order are preserved in the report.

rules.title: Keywords identical after NFKC normalization
rules.description: Two keywords differ only by Unicode compatibility forms (for example full-width and ASCII letters, or ligatures). Reported as a suggestion; originals are never altered.

rules.title: Empty keyword item
rules.description: The Keywords cell contains empty items, e.g. 'sky,,sun', a leading comma or a trailing comma.

rules.title: Keyword contains a non-comma separator
rules.description: HEURISTIC: a keyword contains a semicolon, vertical bar, or a non-ASCII comma (full-width, ideographic or Arabic). Keywords are separated by ASCII commas, so this is probably several keywords that will be read as one.

rules.title: Technical or filler keyword in the first 10
rules.description: HEURISTIC: one of the first 10 keywords looks like technical data or a generic filler term (file type, resolution, camera setting, 'stock photo'). The word list is StockMetaLint's own; it cannot judge relevance and is only a suggestion.
rules.notes: Related Adobe guidance: the CSV requirements page asks contributors not to include technical data in keywords.

rules.title: Same Filename in several rows
rules.description: The same Filename appears in more than one data row, so it is ambiguous which metadata applies.

rules.title: Filenames differ only by case
rules.description: Two Filename values differ only by letter case. On Windows and default macOS file systems they name the same file.

rules.title: Filenames equal after Unicode normalization
rules.description: Two Filename values are canonically equivalent (identical after NFC) but differ in bytes.

rules.title: Identical title used for several files
rules.description: REVIEW: the same title (case- and whitespace-insensitive) is used in several rows. This is not an automatic Adobe rejection; check that each title describes its own asset.

rules.title: Identical keyword sets
rules.description: REVIEW: several rows have exactly the same set of keywords. This is not an automatic rejection; series of similar files often still need individual keywords.

rules.title: Near-duplicate keyword sets
rules.description: HEURISTIC REVIEW: rows with at least 10 keywords share the same set of their first 10 normalized keywords while their full sets differ.

rules.title: Cell could be executed as a spreadsheet formula
rules.description: A cell starts with =, +, -, @, tab or carriage return (or with = + - @ after spaces). If the CSV is opened in a spreadsheet, the cell may be evaluated as a formula. StockMetaLint never writes such cells unescaped in fix output.

rules.title: Bidirectional control or invisible character
rules.description: Text contains bidirectional control characters (e.g. U+202E) or invisible characters (e.g. U+200B) that can disguise what is displayed. In Filename, zero-width joiners are reported too.

rules.title: No asset file matches the Filename
rules.description: With --assets, no file in the asset directory has exactly this name (exact spelling and case).

rules.title: Asset matches only when ignoring case
rules.description: A file matches the Filename only when letter case is ignored. Exact names are required.

rules.title: Asset matches only after Unicode normalization
rules.description: A file matches the Filename only after Unicode normalization (NFC/NFD), typically a name created on macOS.

rules.title: Asset file without a CSV row
rules.description: A file in the asset directory is not referenced by any row, so this CSV gives it no metadata. Hidden files (starting with '.'), Thumbs.db and desktop.ini are ignored.

rules.title: Asset directory has no files
rules.description: The asset directory contains no candidate files (hidden files are ignored).

rules.title: Asset files differ only by case
rules.description: Two files in the asset directory differ only by letter case and collide on case-insensitive file systems.

rules.title: Same asset name in several subdirectories
rules.description: With --recursive, the same file name exists in more than one subdirectory, so the match is ambiguous.

rules.title: Asset symlink points outside the asset directory
rules.description: The matching entry is a symbolic link resolving outside the asset directory. It is not followed or read.

rules.title: Asset symlink is broken
rules.description: The matching entry is a symbolic link whose target does not exist.

rules.title: Asset is not a regular file
rules.description: The matching entry is a directory or special file (FIFO, socket, device), not a regular file.

rules.title: Asset file is empty
rules.description: The matching file has a size of 0 bytes.

rules.title: Release file not found locally
rules.description: With --releases, a release name from the Releases column has no file in that directory with the exact name or the name plus .jpg/.jpeg. Releases are normally uploaded to the platform separately; this only checks your local copy.

rules.title: File content does not match its extension
rules.description: FORMAT CHECK: the file's leading bytes do not match its extension (for example a PNG renamed to .jpg). This validates file format only, not content policy.

rules.title: File type not inspectable
rules.description: FORMAT CHECK: StockMetaLint cannot inspect this extension; the file was matched by name only.

rules.title: Image could not be decoded
rules.description: FORMAT CHECK: Pillow could not decode the image (corrupt or truncated). This validates file format only, not Adobe content policy or quality.

rules.title: Video container could not be read
rules.description: FORMAT CHECK: ffprobe could not read the container or found no video stream.

rules.title: Inspection inconclusive
rules.description: INCONCLUSIVE: an optional inspection tool (Pillow or ffprobe) is unavailable, failed or timed out, so the affected files were not verified. This is not a pass.
